sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Mesa, AZ?
sections.html:
Selling a house in Mesa comes down to three routes: list it with an agent, sell it yourself, or accept a cash purchase. Each route runs through the same Maricopa County deed filing and the same property tax calendar. Mesa is big, with 513,656 residents on the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate, so the street, the school district and the age of the roof change how a sale plays out.

This page covers how Mesa is laid out, which districts serve it, what the desert climate means for a buyer's inspection, the city's short-term rental license, the deed paperwork at the county recorder and the tax dates that matter at closing.

sections.h2: How big is Mesa and what do Census numbers say about its homes?
sections.html:
Mesa is the third most populous city in Arizona, and the Census Bureau puts the median value of an owner-occupied home at $408,000 for 2020 to 2024. The table below pulls the figures a seller is most likely to want when comparing Mesa with a neighboring city.

Owner-occupied housing rate64.4%

Source: Census Bureau QuickFacts.

With 64.4 percent of homes owner-occupied, about one household in three in Mesa rents. That matters if your house has been a rental or if the person buying it plans to rent it out.

sections.h2: Which part of Mesa is the house in, and why does it matter?
sections.html:
Mesa stretches about 18 miles from Price Road in the west to Meridian Road in the east, and Center Street divides it into West Mesa and East Mesa for street numbering. The address tells a buyer at once which half of the city the house is in.

Mesa borders Tempe on the west, the Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community on the north, Chandler, Gilbert and Queen Creek on the south, and Apache Junction on the east. The city's licensing page also warns that a parcel with a Mesa postal address can sit on a Maricopa County island outside Mesa's jurisdiction. Look the parcel up on the city's Explore Mesa map before you assume any city rule applies to it.

School boundaries also split inside the city limits:

  • Mesa Public Schools serves almost all of the city.
  • The southern edge is served by Gilbert Public Schools, Higley Unified and Queen Creek Unified.
  • A small western strip falls under the Tempe Elementary School District and the Tempe Union High School District.

Ask each district for the boundary map before you promise a buyer a particular school.

sections.h2: How did Mesa grow into a city of half a million?
sections.html:
Mesa grew from a Hohokam canal landscape and a Mormon farming settlement into a suburb that now holds more than 500,000 people. The Hohokam dug canals here at least 2,000 years ago, and the first Mesa company of settlers reused some of that canal work, with water flowing by April 1878. Mesa City was registered as a one-square-mile townsite on July 17, 1878, and incorporated in 1883 with about 300 residents.

Military airfields at Falcon Field and Williams Field in the early 1940s brought more people, and air conditioning and aerospace work pushed growth through the 1950s and 1960s. As late as 1960, half of Mesa's residents still earned a living from agriculture.

Wikipedia, citing the city's 2022 annual financial report, lists Mesa Public Schools (7,726 employees), Banner Health (6,826), Boeing (3,945) and the City of Mesa (3,579) as the largest local employers.

sections.h2: How do roads and transit affect a Mesa sale?
sections.html:
Mesa homes sit close to several freeways, which is a selling point you can state plainly in a listing or an offer conversation. U.S. 60, called the Superstition Freeway, crosses the city, Loop 101 runs along the western edge, and Loop 202 passes the north and east sides. Main Street is the main east to west arterial, and Country Club Drive, Gilbert Road and Power Road carry traffic north and south.

Valley Metro light rail covers about four miles of Main Street, from Sycamore to Gilbert Road. Mesa Gateway Airport sits in the southeast corner, and the Polytechnic campus of Arizona State University is in southeast Mesa. Mesa Community College, which Wikipedia describes as the largest of the Maricopa Community Colleges, is also based here.

sections.h2: How does Mesa's desert climate affect selling a house?
sections.html:
Mesa has a hot desert climate, so buyers and inspectors pay attention to cooling equipment and the roof. For East Mesa, the 1991 to 2020 normals show a mean daily high of 105.9 degrees in July, a record high of 121 degrees, and about 10.76 inches of rain across a year. Wet days cluster in January through March and again from July through September.

Before listing, pull together whatever you have:

  • Service records for the air conditioning system.
  • The age and any repair history of the roof.
  • Permit paperwork for patios, additions or a pool.

A seller who can hand over those papers answers the first questions a buyer's inspector will ask.

sections.h2: Do Mesa's short-term rental rules matter when selling?
sections.html:
They matter whenever the house has been rented for 29 days or less at a time. Mesa requires a short-term rental license, and the city issues it only to the property owner. The licensing page lists these conditions:

  • A renewal application and the $250 fee per rental unit must reach the Licensing office at least 45 days before the license expires.
  • The rental unit needs a valid Arizona Transaction Privilege Tax license that lists its location.
  • Neighbors next to and surrounding the unit must be notified, with the Mesa license number, the address and an emergency contact.

If you are selling a house that carries a Mesa short-term rental license, ask the Licensing office what happens to the license at transfer, and tell your buyer what you learn.

sections.h2: How is a Mesa deed recorded at the Maricopa County Recorder?
sections.html:
The deed goes to the Maricopa County Recorder with an Affidavit of Property Value, or with an exemption code written on the document. Under A.R.S. 11-1133, the buyer and seller (or their agents) jointly certify the sale price, the parcel number, the date of sale, how the sale was financed and whether the home will be owner-occupied or rented. The recorder refuses a deed that lacks a complete affidavit unless it carries an exemption notation.

The standard fee is $30 per document, with some exceptions listed on the recorder's fee page. The office at 301 W Jefferson St, Suite 200 in Phoenix is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and the recorder says its staff cannot advise which code fits a deed. In practice a title or escrow company prepares and submits the package.

sections.h2: When are Mesa property taxes due, and how are they handled at closing?
sections.html:
Arizona property tax is paid in two halves, due October 1 and the following March 1. Under A.R.S. 42-18052, the first half goes delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 1 and the second after 5:00 p.m. on May 1. A bill of $100 or less is due in full on October 1 and goes delinquent after December 31.

Today is past November 1, so check with the Maricopa County Treasurer whether the first half on your parcel is paid. The next due date after that is March 1. Ask your title company how the current year's bill is split between you and the buyer.

faqs.q: Does a house sale in Mesa need an Affidavit of Property Value?
faqs.a: Yes, unless the deed qualifies for an exemption code. A.R.S. 11-1133 requires the affidavit to be attached when a deed or sale contract is recorded, and the county recorder refuses a deed without a complete one unless it carries an exemption notation.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Maricopa County?
faqs.a: The standard fee is $30 per document. The Maricopa County Recorder notes that some exceptions apply, so check its recording fees page for the document you are filing.

faqs.q: Is every address with a Mesa mailing address inside Mesa city limits?
faqs.a: No. The city says a parcel on a Maricopa County island can have a Mesa postal address while sitting outside Mesa's jurisdiction. Use the Explore Mesa map or call the Licensing office before assuming a city license or rule applies.

faqs.q: When is the second half of Arizona property tax due?
faqs.a: The second half is due March 1 and goes delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on May 1 of that year. The first half is due October 1 and is delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 1.

faqs.q: Which school district serves a house in Mesa?
faqs.a: Mesa Public Schools serves almost all of the city. The south is served by Gilbert Public Schools, Higley Unified or Queen Creek Unified, and a small western portion by the Tempe districts. Confirm the address with the district.
